subject: Cloud Computing
title: When to Choose SaaS
description: A 60-second lesson on When to Choose SaaS.

hook.text: Your company needs email, project management, and CRM. Building any of these yourself would be insane.

buildup.text: SaaS is the right choice when the problem is well-solved and building it isn't your competitive edge.

discovery.text: Using Gmail instead of running your own email server saves thousands of hours of maintenance.

twist.text: The risk is dependency. When Slack goes down, some companies literally cannot communicate.

climax.text: SaaS makes sense for everything that isn't your core product. Build what's unique, buy the rest.

punchline.text: Don't build what you can buy. Save your energy for what matters.

quiz.question: When is SaaS the right choice for a company?
options: When the capability isn't a competitive advantage and is well-solved by existing products
When the company wants full control over the underlying infrastructure
When data privacy requirements prevent using any external services

details.summary: Choose SaaS for standard business functions like email, CRM, project management, and collaboration where customization needs are moderate. SaaS makes sense when speed of deployment and low operational burden outweigh the need for deep customization.
details.whyItMatters: Adopting SaaS for commodity functions frees engineering resources for core business differentiation. Choosing correctly avoids building what you could simply rent.
takeaways: Best for standard business functions and commodity tools
Ideal when speed of deployment is the top priority
Avoid for highly custom workflows needing deep control

faq.question: When should you build instead of buying SaaS?
faq.answer: Build when the software is a core competitive differentiator, when no SaaS product meets critical requirements, or when data sovereignty prevents using third-party services. For unique business logic that drives revenue, custom development often makes more sense.

faq.question: How do you evaluate SaaS tools?
faq.answer: Assess security certifications, uptime SLAs, data export capabilities, integration APIs, pricing scalability, and vendor financial health. Ensure you can export your data if you need to switch. Trial the product with real workflows before committing.
